title: Java News Roundup: JEPs for JDK 28, Azul Payara, Gatherers4j, Google ADK, Yupiik, Apache Camel CVEs
gist: A weekly Java roundup: three JEPs (Adaptive Heap Sizing for ZGC, faster ZGC startup and warmup, and Structured Concurrency finalized after seven previews) are now targeted for JDK 28; Azul Payara 7.5.0 patches two RCE CVEs; Google ADK for Java/Kotlin adds workflow graph types. The most notable data point is that Apache Camel fixed 38 CVEs, 28 of which were found by Claude as part of Project Glasswing.

insights.claim: The Apache Camel team resolved 38 CVEs across numerous Camel components, 13 rated HIGH and 25 MEDIUM; 28 of the 38 were discovered by Claude as part of Project Glasswing and only 10 came from human security researchers.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: AI models now find most of the disclosed vulnerabilities in a major open-source project, which signals a jump in AI-driven vuln-discovery volume and patching load across the open-source supply chain.
insights.quote: Of the 38 CVEs, 28 have been discovered by Claude as part of Project Glasswing and 10 were reported by security researchers.

insights.claim: Apache Camel developers are urged to upgrade to versions 4.23.0, 4.22.1 or 4.18.5 to pick up the CVE fixes.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Enterprises running Camel face a forced patch cycle, and bursts of AI-found CVEs will increase that kind of remediation work.

insights.claim: Azul Payara 7.5.0 fixes CVE-2026-2586, an RCE through the Administration Console, and CVE-2026-2587, an RCE in server-side template rendering that allows host compromise, persistence and lateral movement.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Critical RCE patches in Jakarta EE app servers show ongoing security exposure in legacy Java middleware.

insights.claim: JEP 546, Adaptive Heap Sizing for ZGC, is targeted for JDK 28 and would let the Z Garbage Collector adjust heap size based on available resources, the application's needs and those of neighboring applications competing for the same resources.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: JVM heaps that resize themselves improve container density and cut over-provisioned cloud memory for Java workloads.
insights.quote: the needs of neighboring applications contending for the same resources
insights.locator: JEP 546, Adaptive Heap Sizing for ZGC

insights.claim: JEP 545, Faster Startup and Warmup with ZGC, is targeted for JDK 28 and makes ZGC acquire and prepare physical memory faster, improving application startup and warmup.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Better JVM startup helps Java compete in serverless and autoscaling environments.

insights.claim: JEP 543, Structured Concurrency, will be finalized unchanged in JDK 28 after seven preview rounds (JDK 21 through JDK 27) and two incubator rounds (JDK 19 and 20).
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: After about five years of iteration, structured concurrency is stable enough for production adoption in JDK 28.

themes.theme: Agent frameworks in the JVM ecosystem

insights.claim: Google ADK for Java 1.12.0 adds workflow graph types (a Node interface, BaseNode and Start classes, and an Edge record) and replaces the deprecated maxInvocations parameter of ContextCacheConfig with cacheIntervals and createHttpOptions.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Google is pushing graph-based agent workflows into enterprise Java, competing with Python-first agent frameworks.

insights.claim: Google ADK for Kotlin 1.4.0 adds an EdgesDsl for building workflow graphs and a ChatCompletions model backend for the OpenAI Chat Completions API and compatible endpoints.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Google's agent kit supports OpenAI's API as a backend, which shows the Chat Completions format becoming the de facto interoperability standard.

insights.claim: Gatherers4j 0.15.0 adds statistical stream gatherers, including movingStatistics, runningStatistics and movingWeightedMean with linear or developer-provided weights.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Small sign of the ecosystem building on the JDK Stream Gatherers API.
